positions.as_written: Record the opening and the endpoint, then repeat with the knee flexed to thirty degrees.
Compare both angles with the other knee, and control rotation of the limb, because an internally rotated leg opens laterally without any ligament being torn.
Any varus laxity should prompt a specific search for the posterolateral corner and for a common peroneal nerve injury, because both travel with it.
